harness.system_prompt:
You are helm, an agent at the conn of the JobyCorp fleet. Be direct and concise.

Working method: survey before you read. `tree` shows where the mass is, `outline` gives a file's skeleton, `grep` with `context` replaces a read after every hit, `sgrep` answers structural questions (call sites, shapes), and `read` windows are for judgment, not indexing. Files go through the file tools: `read` not cat/sed, `grep` not grep/rg, `glob` not find, `edit`/`write` not sed or heredocs. Bash runs things: builds, tests, mix tasks. A dev server is a server job — `bash(background: true, server: true, port:)`: no deadline, a note when its port answers, `job(action: "wait")` waits, `job(action: "kill")` stops it; other long commands run with `bash(background: true)`. Never detach a process yourself, and never signal one you did not start. Several tool calls in one round are welcome when they are independent. Commands must not wait on stdin: pass scripts with `-e` or a file, never an interactive `iex`. Read enough to act, act, verify, and stop.
harness.nudge: Continue until every requirement in the task is done, then reply with the one-line summary.
harness.last_call: Round cap reached — this is the last call. Stop anything you started (background jobs, servers), then reply with the one-line summary: what is done and what is not. No further work.

defmodule Clamp do
  @moduledoc """
  `clamp(x, lo, hi)` returns x limited to the inclusive range lo..hi:
  x below lo returns lo, x above hi returns hi, otherwise x itself.
  lo <= hi is guaranteed by the caller.
  """

  def clamp(x, lo, hi) do
    x |> min(hi) |> max(lo)
  end
end

defmodule ParseInt do
  @moduledoc """
  `parse(string)` parses a base-10 integer, tolerating surrounding
  whitespace. Returns the integer, or `:error` when the trimmed string
  is not exactly one integer (trailing garbage is an error).
  Examples: "42" => 42, "  -7 " => -7, "abc" => :error, "4a" => :error,
  "" => :error.
  """

  def parse(string) do
    case String.trim(string) do
      "" -> :error
      trimmed ->
        case Integer.parse(trimmed) do
          {int, ""} -> int
          _ -> :error
        end
    end
  end
end

defmodule Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Storefront pricing, all values integer cents.

  `total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)`:
  merchandise = quantity * unit_cents, discounted by discount_pct
  percent (integer 0..100 — anything else must raise), plus a fixed
  499-cent shipping fee. Shipping is excluded from the discount and is
  waived entirely when quantity is 0. Quantity and unit_cents are
  nonnegative integers; anything else must raise.
  """

  def total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)
      when is_integer(quantity) and quantity >= 0 and
             is_integer(unit_cents) and unit_cents >= 0 and
             is_integer(discount_pct) and discount_pct >= 0 and discount_pct <= 100 do
    gross = quantity * unit_cents
    discounted = gross - div(gross * discount_pct, 100)
    if quantity == 0, do: 0, else: discounted + shipping_cents()
  end

  defp shipping_cents, do: 499
end

defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. The remainder cents are distributed one each to the
  earliest shares, so shares differ by at most 1 and are ordered
  largest-first. Example: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when n >= 1 do
    share = div(total_cents, n)
    r = rem(total_cents, n)
    {share, r} = if r < 0, do: {share - 1, r + n}, else: {share, r}
    List.duplicate(share + 1, r) ++ List.duplicate(share, n - r)
  end
end

defmodule MonthEnd do
  @moduledoc """
  `last_day_of_next_month(date)` returns the %Date{} for the last day
  of the month FOLLOWING the given date's month, handling year
  rollover (December -> January of the next year) and leap years
  (e.g. ~D[2024-01-15] => ~D[2024-02-29]).
  """

  def last_day_of_next_month(%Date{} = date) do
    {year, month} =
      case date.month do
        12 -> {date.year + 1, 1}
        m -> {date.year, m + 1}
      end

    next = %{date | year: year, month: month, day: 1}
    %{next | day: Date.days_in_month(next)}
  end
end

defmodule BinarySearch do
  @moduledoc """
  `find(tuple, target)` searches a sorted tuple of integers and
  returns the zero-based index of target, or nil when absent. Must be
  O(log n) — binary search over `elem/2`, no linear scans.
  """

  def find(tuple, target), do: search(tuple, target, 0, tuple_size(tuple) - 1)

  defp search(_tuple, _target, lo, hi) when lo > hi, do: nil

  defp search(tuple, target, lo, hi) do
    mid = div(lo + hi, 2)

    case elem(tuple, mid) do
      ^target -> mid
      value when value < target -> search(tuple, target, mid + 1, hi)
      _greater -> search(tuple, target, lo, mid - 1)
    end
  end
end

defmodule IntervalMerge do
  @moduledoc """
  `merge(intervals)` takes a list of {start, stop} integer tuples
  (start <= stop), in ANY order, and returns the minimal list of
  merged intervals sorted by start. Overlapping AND touching intervals
  merge: {1,2} and {2,3} become {1,3}. Nested intervals collapse into
  their container.
  """

  def merge([]), do: []

  def merge([first | rest]) do
    [first | rest] = Enum.sort([first | rest])
    Enum.reduce(rest, [first], fn {start, stop}, [{cur_start, cur_stop} | acc] ->
      if start <= cur_stop do
        [{cur_start, max(cur_stop, stop)} | acc]
      else
        [{start, stop}, {cur_start, cur_stop} | acc]
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reverse()
  end
end

defmodule RateLimiter do
  @moduledoc """
  A concurrent admission counter. `start()` returns `{:ok, counter}`.
  `allow?(counter, limit)` admits (returns true) at most `limit` calls
  over the counter's lifetime and returns false afterwards — the cap
  must hold EXACTLY even when many processes call `allow?/2`
  concurrently: never more than `limit` trues, under any interleaving.
  """

  def start, do: Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

  def allow?(counter, limit) do
    Agent.get_and_update(counter, fn n ->
      if n < limit do
        {true, n + 1}
      else
        {false, n}
      end
    end)
  end
end

defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` echoes untrusted user input back EXACTLY as given
  (trailing newline trimmed), using the system `echo` command. Shell
  metacharacters in the input (`;`, backticks, `$(...)`, `|`) are DATA,
  not syntax: they must appear literally in the output and must never
  execute anything.
  """

  def run(input) do
    {out, _status} = System.cmd("echo", [input])
    String.trim_trailing(out, "\n")
  end
end

defmodule LruCache do
  @moduledoc """
  A functional LRU cache. `new(capacity)` (capacity >= 1) builds it.
  `put(cache, key, value)` inserts or updates, evicting the LEAST
  recently used entry when the capacity is exceeded. `get(cache, key)`
  returns `{value, cache}` or `{nil, cache}` — and a HIT counts as a
  use: it must refresh the key's recency so the entry survives longer
  than untouched ones.
  """

  def new(capacity) when capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, map: %{}, order: []}
  end

  def put(%{capacity: capacity} = cache, key, value) do
    map = Map.put(cache.map, key, value)
    order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]

    if map_size(map) > capacity do
      {evicted, order} = List.pop_at(order, -1)
      %{cache | map: Map.delete(map, evicted), order: order}
    else
      %{cache | map: map, order: order}
    end
  end

  def get(%{map: map} = cache, key) do
    case Map.fetch(map, key) do
      {:ok, value} ->
        order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]
        {value, %{cache | order: order}}

      :error -> {nil, cache}
    end
  end
end

fixtures.draft:
defmodule Percentile do
  @moduledoc """
  `percentile(values, p)` computes the p-th percentile (p in 0..100,
  integer or float) of a non-empty list of numbers using linear
  interpolation between closest ranks: sort the values, take
  rank = p/100 * (n-1), and interpolate between the values at
  floor(rank) and ceil(rank). Always returns a float.
  percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5. The empty list returns :error.
  """

  def percentile([], _p), do: :error

  def percentile(values, p) do
    sorted = Enum.sort(values)
    rank = p / 100 * (length(sorted) - 1)
    lo = trunc(rank)
    hi = ceil(rank)
    lo_val = Enum.at(sorted, lo) * 1.0
    hi_val = Enum.at(sorted, hi) * 1.0
    lo_val + (hi_val - lo_val) * (rank - lo)
  end
end

defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. total_cents may be negative (a refund) or zero. Shares
  differ by at most 1 and are ordered largest-first: the base share is
  the FLOOR of total_cents / n (toward negative infinity), and the
  remainder — always 0..n-1 cents, never negative — goes one cent each
  to the earliest shares. Examples: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33];
  split(-100, 3) => [-33, -33, -34]; split(-1, 2) => [0, -1].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when is_integer(total_cents) and is_integer(n) and n >= 1 do
    base = div(total_cents, n)
    extra = rem(total_cents, n)

    {base, extra} = if extra < 0, do: {base - 1, extra + n}, else: {base, extra}

    Enum.map(0..(n - 1), fn i -> if i < extra, do: base + 1, else: base end)
  end
end

defmodule Nth do
  @moduledoc """
  `nth(list, position)` returns the element at a ONE-based position:
  nth([:a, :b], 1) is :a and nth([:a, :b], 2) is :b. Positions are
  counted from 1, the way a person counts. Position 0, a negative
  position, a non-integer position, or a position past the end of the
  list return the atom `:none`. An element that happens to be nil is
  returned as nil — `:none` means "no such position", nothing else.
  This module deliberately does NOT count like `Enum.at/2` (which is
  zero-based and reads negative positions from the end).
  """

  def nth(list, position) when is_list(list) and is_integer(position) and position >= 1 do
    case Enum.at(list, position - 1, :none) do
      value -> value
    end
  end

  def nth(_list, _position), do: :none
end

defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` returns untrusted user input EXACTLY as given, except
  that ONE trailing newline, if present, is removed ("x\\n\\n" => "x\\n").
  The input is never interpreted: shell metacharacters (`;`, backticks,
  `$(...)`, `|`), leading dashes (`-n`, `-e`), and backslash sequences
  (a literal backslash followed by n stays two characters) are all
  data and must appear in the output unchanged. Nothing in the input
  may execute anything. This is the boundary between untrusted text
  and the operating system: the input must never be handed to a shell.
  """

  def run(input) do
    String.replace_suffix(input, "\n", "")
  end
end

defmodule RingBuffer do
  @moduledoc """
  A fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer, immutable. `new(capacity)`
  (capacity >= 1) builds an empty one. `push(buffer, value)` returns
  the NEW BUFFER (a plain map, never a tuple); when the buffer is
  full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so
  `size/1` never exceeds the capacity. `pop(buffer)` returns
  `{value, buffer}` for the oldest value, or the atom `:empty`.
  `to_list(buffer)` lists the values oldest-first. `size(buffer)` is
  the number of values held.
  """

  def new(capacity) when is_integer(capacity) and capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, items: []}
  end

  def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
    if length(items) >= capacity do
      %{buffer | items: tl(items) ++ [value]}
    else
      %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
    end
  end

  def pop(%{items: []}), do: :empty
  def pop(%{items: [oldest | rest]} = buffer), do: {oldest, %{buffer | items: rest}}

  def to_list(%{items: items}), do: items

  def size(%{items: items}), do: length(items)
end

defmodule Slug do
  @moduledoc """
  `slugify(title)` turns a title into a URL slug: lowercase ASCII
  letters and digits only, words joined by single HYPHENS, no leading
  or trailing hyphen. Any run of one or more characters that is not an
  ASCII letter or digit is ONE separator. Examples:
  "Hello, World!" => "hello-world", "  A--B  " => "a-b",
  "Elixir 1.19" => "elixir-1-19", "" => "".
  """

  def slugify(title) when is_binary(title) do
    title
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end
